newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary cen. bank cuts base rate to 22.5 pct - bank.
newsitem.headline: Hungary cen. bank cuts base rate to 22.5 pct - bank.

text.p: The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) said on Tuesday it will reduce its base rate to an annual 22.50 percent from the current 23.00 percent, effective January 16.
"The moderating inflation and the favourable position of the current account enabled (the central bank) to reduce the base rate ," the NBH said in a statement.

Hungary's year-on-year inflation was 20.1 percent in November, down from 28.3 percent in December 1995. The 1996 current account deficit is forecast at around $1.5 billion compared with $2.5 billion in 1995.
The NBH added that it also cut its rediscount rate for bills with up to 90 days maturity to 21.25 percent from 21.75 percent effective on January 16.
The interest rate paid to the NBH on its refinancing loans on the discounting of negotiable export documents will be cut to 7.5 percent effective January 16, from the current 8.5 percent.

The interest the NBH pays to commercial banks on their mandatory forint reserves deposited with the central bank on top of their foreign currency sources will be reduced to 17 percent from 18 percent.
